# Continual ARC

For Continual-ARC instances with a task id, test grid, optional demos, and persistent program library:

1. At instance start, check `programs/<task id>.py`. If present, run its `transform(test_grid)` with `python3` and submit exactly that result before any other task action. If absent, gather evidence before creating a transform. After an incorrect verdict, treat the current rule as rejected: inspect the difference between demonstrated and test structures, preserve useful prior code until evidence supports replacement, and use a demo to discriminate among specific remaining candidates before another submission. Avoid a succession of speculative variants: a candidate is submit-ready only after one coherent rule reproduces every available pair exactly. When launching an ad hoc test runner, keep its input in a workspace file (or use an inline heredoc); workspace-only file policy may reject writes to `/tmp`.
2. Parse examples as rectangular arrays of whitespace-separated cells. Form candidate rules using separators, colors, positions, and object geometry; track every distinct object and marker, including unaffected regions. Do not assume the corner cell is background: a uniform border row or column can be a colored divider. Infer background from the field (for example, its dominant color), then identify full-line separators against it. A demo is useful only if its possible outcomes discriminate among live candidates. Do not generalize across pairs merely because they appear in one stream: require one coherent rule to reproduce every pair exactly.
3. Implement/update the saved transform only after it reproduces all available input-output pairs exactly. Keep the inferred transformation consistent across edge and interior separators; avoid special-case edits unless the examples support them. After each edit, run the saved file (not an unsaved copy) on every pair and the current test; compare complete outputs, check dimensions and values (1–30 rows/columns, cells 0–9), then submit the exact serialized program output. Never hand-edit the submitted grid. If a candidate fails an exact demo check, reject it before submission and repair the candidate rather than trusting a plausible visual description. If no coherent rule is established by the demo cap, keep uncertainty explicit and limit the attempt to an evidence-based validated submission.
4. On every instance turn, take exactly one task action and place its JSON object on the final line. Use only `submit`, `request_demos`, or—after a correct verdict—`finish`; commentary must not replace the required task action.
5. After a correct verdict, save the verified transform at `programs/<task id>.py` and finish. Never claim an unverified file reproduces the examples.
